label: copy phase: input w while outputting l (late in the recall)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and only when the input token is w (about 90% of mass) or l (about 10%). The core case is the w-then-l bigram being copied: the input is w (the model echoing back original token recall_idx-1) and the current output is l. Activation is strongest late in the recall (recall_idx 6-8, final one or two outputs, L=9 holds 66% of mass). Top examples are all of the form ... w l <DEL> ... [w] with w at original position 7. It never fires in the original or delimiter phases, or on any input other than w or l. Weak activations also appear on w inputs followed by other outputs (w, z, q, x) and on l inputs, which caps recall. Early w->l pairs (recall_idx < 4) mostly do not fire. Dev scores: precision 0.69, recall 0.45, F1 0.54, mass recall 0.64.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: w, l, -, 0, g, u; least: z, r, s, <DEL>) and the token being output (most: l, w, z, q, o, x; least: p, u, t, -); timing cues that raise it most: t=17, recall_idx=8, L=9 & t=17.
